approachQuestion.prompt: An immutable token list encodes a Boolean expression. Atoms are TRUE and FALSE. A compound is ALL, OPEN, one or more comma-separated expressions, CLOSE, or ANY with the same grammar. ALL is true exactly when every child is true; ANY when at least one child is true. The root is one expression. The n tokens, 1 <= n <= 200,000, are guaranteed valid. Return one Boolean. Choose a method minimizing worst-case total processing time. Input: [ALL,OPEN,TRUE,COMMA,ANY,OPEN,FALSE,COMMA,TRUE,CLOSE,CLOSE]. Output: true. There are no other operators.

options.text: Scan with frames storing compound kind and running aggregate, initialized true for ALL and false for ANY. Fold each completed child into its parent; on CLOSE pop the completed aggregate and fold it upward, or return it at the root.
options.feedback: Each frame retains only the operator and its accumulated child result; closing a compound produces exactly one child result for its parent.

options.text: Keep one current operator that is overwritten whenever ALL or ANY appears, and combine every atom using it.
options.feedback: ALL(TRUE,ANY(FALSE,TRUE),FALSE) is false; forgetting the outer ALL can leave the final FALSE combined with ANY and incorrectly return true.

options.text: Ignore compound boundaries and return true whenever any atom is TRUE.
options.feedback: ALL(TRUE,FALSE) must be false, but this method returns true.

options.text: For each compound, scan its full token span again to locate children and evaluate their results recursively without memoization.
options.feedback: This follows the grammar and is correct, but deeply nested compounds repeatedly inspect the same token spans rather than retaining the active folds.

feedback.reason: Nested compounds need separate pending aggregates because each parent combines its children with its own operator.
details: A frame stores ALL or ANY and its running Boolean. An atom supplies a completed child directly. Closing a frame supplies its final Boolean to the next outer frame; the root value becomes the result.

Each compound frame combines completed child values using its own ALL or ANY operation. Closing a frame passes one Boolean to its parent, preserving nested boundaries without retaining every child expression.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For fold-boolean-frames, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: The input is immutable and excluded from auxiliary space. Returned output is excluded, but all working buffers count even if later copied into output.
Fixed-size integers, characters, indices and comparisons take constant time. Arithmetic is unit cost under the stated range guarantee.
Use an iterative implementation with a preallocated n-entry array and a top index: push and pop take constant time. No recursion, hashing, or hidden whole-buffer copies occur.
Materializing output takes time proportional to its length; no persistent snapshots or string concatenation are used.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each token and frame transition is processed once, with depth-bounded live state.
details: Each token is consumed once and each frame pushed and popped once. A chain of nested one-child compounds produces linear depth, so the iterative frame stack uses O(n) auxiliary space. Output is one excluded Boolean.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A chain of nested one-child ALL/ANY compounds retains a linear number of unfinished operator frames.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each atom contributes once and each compound frame combines child results and closes once; earlier subexpressions are not replayed.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A late child can determine a compound value in a valid worst case, requiring all expression tokens to be read.
